input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: The second § 12.4 imposes a non-compete on Customer that runs during the term and for twenty-four months afterwards, covering any competing product or service in any territory. That is walk-away territory under NONCOMPETE (post-term restriction longer than 12 months and undefined scope) and fails every fallback element: no named product, post-term application, 24 months, and no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions. It also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no non-compete commitment. The separate no-hire sentence in the first § 12.4 is a non-solicitation term and is not flagged here. We took the preferred position by converting the prohibition into a confirmation of Customer's freedom of action, which is the shortest edit and removes the conflict with § 12.3.

ops.oldText: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
ops.newText: Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a non-compete or field-of-use restriction on our business, so we have replaced the prohibition in the second § 12.4 with a confirmation of our freedom of action; it also contradicted § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we made no non-compete commitment. If Vendor needs protection, we could discuss a restriction limited to a single named competing product, during the term only and capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for our internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Remove the two-year post-term non-compete on Customer in § 12.4 and confirm Customer's freedom of action

mappings.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
